refresh_policy.website_task_rule: create one asynchronous projectless website task for one material refresh goal; task-id return is the dispatch receipt; never block the source conversation or reuse a completed task
refresh_policy.full_refresh_rule: the current website AI task iterates enabled projects in registry order; unchanged projects remain byte-identical
refresh_policy.fact_collector_boundary: scripts and providers collect evidence and verify contracts; they never write narrative content or decide materiality
refresh_policy.publication_boundary: source project publication completes first; website refresh is a separate asynchronous post-publication task and cannot block or roll back the source transaction
refresh_policy.publication_mode: after the accepted four-project MVP, verified registered refreshes automatically commit, normal-push existing PUBLIC main, wait for Pages and read back the deployed commit unless the owner explicitly holds publication
refresh_policy.task_creation_threshold: create a website task only when the source owner confirms a material displayed fact or explanation would become wrong; path matches alone are candidates
refresh_policy.small_change_policy: do not create an asynchronous task for formatting, refactors, timestamps, hash-only drift, blocked candidates already shown accurately, or other changes that do not alter a user decision
refresh_policy.default_change_policy: no website change unless the existing page would make a material user judgment wrong
refresh_policy.anti_append_policy: replace, merge or remove current content in place; never append refresh logs, duplicate sections, cards or timeline entries because a refresh ran
refresh_policy.evolution_policy: record only important product stages; one entry may cover a date or date range and may merge multiple related changes
refresh_policy.rule_refresh_boundary: Rules use only the verified current E release; dirty or unreleased source never overwrites it and does not block unrelated project refreshes
refresh_policy.bundle_budget_semantics: the shared-runtime, shared-CSS and compact-search numbers are current anti-bloat review thresholds, not permanent content ceilings; when measured smoothness and semantic fidelity cannot be preserved below them, audit real duplication and wall-clock cost, record the evidence, and apply only the smallest justified increase
refresh_policy.bundle_scaling_policy: build every route with complete narrative HTML before enhancement; keep shared interaction JavaScript, shared CSS and the generated search projection bounded; emit at most the next non-compatibility route as a static document prefetch, retain pointer/focus intent prefetch, and use native directory-document navigation; never delete required content, add click-time imports or fetches, or shift rendering latency to clicks
